summary: Quaffing the uncursed monster-detection potion reaches the unported potion.c:peffect_monster_detection() branch. C scans the live monster list and, when monsters exist, maps them, reports their presence, allows map browsing, and returns 0; the caller then exercises Wisdom and continues through potion identification and consumption. JS still throws at peffects() dispatch, and its existing monster_detect() helper also rejects the non-null potion object this source path passes.

source.branch: POT_MONSTER_DETECTION or SPE_DETECT_MONSTERS. The full function first handles blessed objects by updating potion knowledge flags and HDetect_monsters timeout, clearing invisible glyphs and recalculating the map, then using persistent see_monsters() and returning 0 when not swallowed or underwater. Otherwise it calls monster_detect(otmp, 0): return 1 means no monster and is propagated to peffects() for an early return; return 0 means detection succeeded, so the function exercises Wisdom and returns 0. In this recording the potion is uncursed (mkobj.c:1074-1080 calls blessorcurse(otmp, 4); the recorded rn2(4)=3 does not bless or curse it), the hero is not swallowed or underwater, and a live hostile grid bug is present, so the object-specific detector path is reached.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:1333-1370 peffects() dispatches POT_MONSTER_DETECTION/SPE_DETECT_MONSTERS; a nonzero effect result returns 1, while zero falls through to peffects() returning -1 at line 1424.

nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:618-640 dopotion() consumes peffects() result: a nonnegative result short-circuits the identification/useup tail; -1 proceeds through potion identification and useup(). dodrink() calls dopotion() at potion.c:614 after item selection.
JS production path is js/cmd.js:3363-3364 runQuaffCommand() -> js/potion.js:dodrink() -> dopotion() -> peffects(); js/potion.js:1175-1177 currently throws at this dispatch.
dependencies: nethack-c/upstream/src/detect.c:797-861 monster_detect(otmp, 0): filters dead monsters and dungeon guardians not on the level; if none remain, optionally calls strange_feeling(otmp) and returns 1. With live monsters it maps them, optionally wakes helpless monsters when otmp is cursed, displays “You sense the presence of monsters.”, uses a persistent map window only for a blessed object on an unconstrained map (otherwise browse_map()), redisplays the map, then returns 0. Its inverted result is consumed directly by peffect_monster_detection(); JS js/detect.js:355-366 currently supports only otmp=null and throws for a potion object.

The other full-function branch uses gp.potion_nothing/gp.potion_unkn, Detect_monsters, HDetect_monsters, incr_itimeout(), rn1()/rn2(), unmap_object(), newsym(), see_monsters(), and exercise(A_WIS, TRUE); the blessed non-swallowed/underwater branch returns 0 after persistent detection without calling monster_detect().

evidence: The canonical queue entry and saved v7 evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260926122253-v7.json identify synthetic/v7/monster-detection-potion-select2 with 1 remaining screen and 53 recorded steps. The evaluation reports 52/53 screens and 52/53 cursors matched, all 2776/2776 RNG calls matched, and the queue’s first mismatch is a stop at step 52: JS refuses quaffing because peffect_monster_detection() is unported.

The C recording challenges/cases/v7/monster-detection-potion-select2.session.json records key o at segment 0 step 52 after q, ?, o selection. C displays “You sense the presence of monsters.” with the mapped grid bug and map-browser --More-- prompt; this step has no RNG calls. The recording ends at that prompt, so the subsequent detector return and potion tail are established by source control flow, not by a later captured input.

Upstream potion.c:914-951 is the complete peffect_monster_detection() body. It distinguishes blessed persistent detection from the ordinary detector path, handles swallowed/underwater fallthrough, propagates monster_detect()’s 1=none result, and exercises Wisdom only after successful detection. potion.c:1333-1370 and :1424 show how peffects() consumes the result; potion.c:618-640 shows dopotion() short-circuit versus potion identification/useup.

Upstream detect.c:797-861 establishes monster_detect()’s return contract and object-specific effects. The saved recipe challenges/cases/v7/monster-detection-potion-select2.recipe.session.json creates a hostile grid bug and wishes for a monster-detection potion; the recorded mkobj trace has rn2(4)=3 at mkobj.c:1846, so blessorcurse() leaves the potion uncursed. The same detector helper currently exists at js/detect.js:355-401 only for a null object and explicitly throws for non-null objects; js/potion.js:1175-1177 is the immediate stop site.
